data.body:
CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: an allowlist .gitignore on the tickets branch.

Idea: replace the current denylist .gitignore with an allowlist ('/*' plus re-includes for
ticket-id dirs, jira-* dirs and the six store dotfiles) so nothing non-ticket-shaped can be
committed.

TESTED both vectors in a scratch repo rather than reasoning about it:
  A) agent runs 'git add -A' with source present  -> gitignore BLOCKS it (source not staged)
  B) 'git stash pop' from another branch          -> gitignore does NOT block it; the index
     still conflicted with 2 unmerged entries, reproducing this bug WITH the allowlist active
Reason: .gitignore governs what git auto-adds for UNTRACKED files. A stash/merge writes INDEX
entries for paths that were tracked where the stash was created, and gitignore has no
authority there. Vector B is the one that actually wedged the store.

REJECTED because it trades a LOUD failure for a SILENT one. Any future store file added at the
top level — as .store-compat.json once was — would be invisibly ignored rather than committed,
and the symptom would present as 'the feature does not work' rather than 'the file was not
tracked'. That silent-failure shape is exactly what made this session's three bugs expensive:
each was detectable but nothing was looking.

Vector A is better addressed by the maintenance entrypoint AC (agents stop needing raw git at
all) than by a branch-level trap. The wedge vector is already closed twice over: the tracker is
now a standalone clone (no shared stash stack), and the foreign-path bucket heals the index if
it ever recurs by any route.

Decision: do not add the allowlist. Recorded so it is not re-proposed.
